analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials 10.26.26 10.30.26 Weekend Edition
key_insights: Industrials rose 210bps on the week, taking the month to date above 300bps. Materials rose by a similar amount on the week but less on the month. Both outperformed broader markets, which fell 50bps and were weighed down by tech.
Q3 earnings season has reached its peak, with half of the desk's coverage reported. By subsector, defense, aerospace and autos led, while transports, data center and airlines lagged.

Top single-stock gainers were mostly under-owned names with better earnings: HAYW +27% (pool end market showing modest improvement), BAH +14% (more a short squeeze across defense and Fed IT than earnings), TXT +12% (no charge taken with Q3), IP +9% (company-specific turnaround signs) and FTV up a similar amount on a better Q3 and guide update.
Worst performers on weaker earnings: OI -22%, DAN -15%, transports TFII, LSTR and CHRW down 12-14%, and BA -9% after lowering expectations for the timing of its free cash flow goals.

AI/data center industrial valuation is the topical debate, including whether NVT should trade cheaper than OTIS. The bull side is that AI-related industrials grow much faster than the rest of the sector and have secular exposure. The bear side is that growth may be peaking (NVT Q3 orders were below organic growth) and that names without a recurring service revenue tail face a possible cliff.

The desk attributes the recent sell-off in power, electrical equipment and E&C names to the NVDA multiple comparison. NVDA derated starting in 2022 while these industrials reached all-time-high multiples and earnings estimates only months ago. The desk says a bottom is forming but, if NVDA is the right comparison, there is still some way to go.

Prime brokerage: global industrials was the most net sold global sector by dollars this week, net sold for the 3rd straight week and in 5 of the last 6 weeks. It also saw the largest percentage de-grossing in 3 months, driven by long sales outpacing short covers.
Next week brings the US midterms, ISM, class 8 truck orders, auto sales and the last heavy week of Q3 earnings. The desk previews 10 reports: BALL, ETN, EXPD, EMR, GWW, RRX, APD, CMI, PH and ROK.
The desk likes ETN into earnings and has been constructive on EXPD into its mid-November analyst day. It calls APD its preferred name within industrial gases.
EMR and ROK are battlegrounds around fiscal 2027 guidance and the process versus discrete automation debate. EMR vs ROK has been a popular pair trade that has worked.

Industrial distributors have been thematic beneficiaries of rising inflation fears. GWW is up 36% year to date, and the desk expects a FAST-like print with a strong Q3 but a slower September exit rate and gross margin pressure from mix.

market_movers.rationale: Desk likes ETN into the Nov 3 report. It sees an idiosyncratic rate-of-change story with data center exposure that is meaningful but not excessive. The stock is down from $460 to $370 since July but has outperformed peers.

Desk has been constructive into the mid-November analyst day, with earnings a potential positive catalyst. Air, ocean and customs volumes are expected to be strong, though European peer reports set a high bar.
Desk calls APD its preferred name within industrial gases. It sees more upside than downside to consensus fiscal 2027 growth of 7% versus 12% in 2026, and valuation remains reasonable.
Short interest is at highs in BALL and at lows in CCK, which sets up a possible squeeze on good news. Near-term price/cost pressure and an expected Q4 volume slowdown are the offsets.

sector_views.rationale: Growth is faster and secular, but orders are below organic growth at NVT and durability is debated. The desk sees the NVDA derating as the template for the recent sell-off.
Distributors have been thematic beneficiaries of rising inflation fears. The desk flags elevated GWW valuation and margin pressure from mix.

earnings_insights: BALL: reports Tue Nov 3 pre-market around 6am, call at 8:30am. Implied move 4%, stock red in six of the last eight reports. EPS growth year to date is tracking ahead of the 10% goal but is set to slow in Q3/Q4. Watch volume, capacity, price/cost and an early 2027 look.

ETN: reports Tue Nov 3 pre-market at 6:30am, call at 11am. Implied move 5%. Last quarter the stock rose 7% after eight red reports in the prior nine. A full-year update and an early 2027 end-market read are expected.

EXPD: reports Tue Nov 3 pre-market around 8:30am, no call. Implied move 5%, stock up in five of the last eight reports. Air, ocean and customs are expected to be strong. Bulls want higher estimates and a meaningful analyst day, while bears point to end-market normalization.

EMR: reports Wed Nov 4 pre-market, call at 8:30am. Implied move 6%, stock up three quarters in a row. Consensus fiscal 2027 EPS growth is 11% versus 9%, and topline growth is 6% versus 5%. Trailing three-month underlying orders in fiscal Q3 accelerated to 7%. Short interest has come down notably.

GWW: reports Wed Nov 4 pre-market at 8am, call at 11am. Implied move 4%, stock up three of the last four prints. The desk expects strong Q3 topline with a slower September exit rate, gross margins pressured by mix, and some one-time Q3 benefits.

RRX: reports Tue Nov 3 pre-market at 7am, call at 10am. Implied move 9%, with double-digit declines in each of the last two quarters. Consensus earnings growth for 2027 is 21% versus 10% this year (which includes an IEEPA benefit). A new CFO is yet to be named and this is fiscal Q3, so visibility on the 2027 guide may be limited.

APD: reports Thu Nov 5 pre-market at 6am, call at 8am. Implied move 5%. This is fiscal Q4, so a full-year 2027 guide is due. Stock moved from $270 to $315 in October. Key items are the macro update, margins and the NEOM project.

CMI: reports Thu Nov 5 pre-market at 7:30am, call at 10am. Implied move 6%, stock down two of the last three prints. The company has missed in recent quarters and class 8 truck orders hit a recent low. Over $8 of Q3 EPS does not look like a lock, and mid-teens 2027 EBITDA growth is expected to hold in consensus.

PH: reports Thu Nov 5 pre-market at 7:30am, call at 11am. Implied move 6%, stock green in 14 of the last 17 quarters. This is fiscal Q1, so little change to 2027 guidance is expected. Q1 was guided conservatively and consensus is there. Orders have been strong and accelerating.

ROK: reports Thu Nov 5 pre-market at 7am, call at 8:30am. Implied move 8%. The company needs to guide fiscal 2027, and investors are skeptical and net short. The stock has been rangebound since fiscal Q3 despite consistent beats and raises.
Q3 reported already: TXT took no charge with its Q3 report, and FTV and HAYW delivered better Q3 results. OI, DAN and the transports TFII, LSTR and CHRW reported worse results and fell sharply.

risk_factors: AI/data center industrial growth may be peaking, with a possible cliff for names without recurring service revenue.
Further multiple derating if the NVDA comparison holds.
Continued net selling and de-grossing in global industrials.
Input cost inflation squeezing margins, for example price/cost pressure at BALL and gross margin pressure at GWW.
Weak class 8 truck orders weigh on CMI.
Delayed free cash flow timing, as seen at BA.
Fiscal 2027 guidance disappointments at EMR, ROK and APD.
Sell-the-news risk around the EXPD analyst day.
vol_and_positioning: Prime: global industrials was the most net sold global sector by dollars for the 3rd straight week and in 5 of the last 6 weeks, with the largest percentage de-grossing in 3 months.
Implied earnings moves for next week: RRX 9%, ROK 8%, EMR 6%, CMI 6%, PH 6%, ETN 5%, EXPD 5%, APD 5%, BALL 4%, GWW 4%.
BALL short interest is at highs and CCK is at lows, setting up a possible squeeze in BALL on good news.
GWW short interest is at the high end but not extreme, at 5 days to cover and 3% of float.
APD days to cover are near recent highs, driven as much by lower liquidity as by more shares short.
ROK positioning is sharply lower and net short, which has helped it outperform other cyclicals.
EMR short interest has come down notably.
BAH's rally was more a function of a short squeeze across defense and Fed IT than of earnings.
PH has traded heavy on crowding and aerospace exposure in recent months.
geopolitical: US midterm elections are next week.
IEEPA tariff-driven benefit in RRX earnings, which flatters this year's growth base.
Easy comparisons in the Middle East support EMR's 2027 topline.
NEOM project in the Middle East is a focus for APD, with a wide range of investor expectations.
